A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChatGarment research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support reliable matching across reorganized sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, garment-editing, and text-generation experiments, plus backbone and training-data ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds runtime measurements and qualitative reconstruction examples.

M1.justification: Equation (1) adds a mask to the numeric L1 loss, excluding irrelevant numeric attributes. The backbone, LoRA training, numeric projection layer, and overall garment pipeline remain unchanged. This revises the stated objective without establishing that training was rerun.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated tasks remain the same, including Dress4D/CloSe reconstruction, garment editing, text generation, sketches, and simulation control. The new single-turn examples illustrate image-only reconstruction already evaluated through LLaVA-I in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and S10–S11. DressCode is reorganized within the baseline description but remains in the same reconstruction, editing, and generation comparisons.

E3.justification: Section S3.5 adds a three-stage runtime evaluation on an A100 GPU. Existing training budgets and benchmark metrics are retained. CloSe filtering is described differently, but the PDFs do not establish that its evaluated sample set changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds a runtime bottleneck analysis and qualitative cases illustrating direct, single-turn reconstruction and GarmentCodeRC's representational capacity. Existing backbone/data ablations, simulation-control examples, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests. The added runtime measurements introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports 12.1 seconds for LLM decoding, 3.5 seconds for GarmentCode generation, and 33.9 seconds for stitching, alongside additional qualitative examples. Numerical results and rankings in Tables 1–4 and S10–S11 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1) changes the mathematical definition of the numeric loss through the added mask. The simulation-control equations (2)–(5) are unchanged, and neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain unified multimodal garment estimation, generation and editing, VLM-generated JSON, refined GarmentCode, and automatic dataset construction. Reworded impact language and additional supporting examples do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v3 attributes some failures to LLM hallucinations, explicitly states that GarmentCodeRC cannot represent details such as zippers and pockets, and identifies stitching as the runtime bottleneck. Its future-work discussion adds RAG, in-context learning, and post-training.

D1.justification: The abstract changes reported code/data availability from forthcoming to available, and S1.1 adds a skirt JSON example. Conversely, v3 omits ContourCraft fine-tuning, 60-frame interpolation, default stitching settings, and failed-reconstruction exclusion details. Core training settings remain documented in S1; these omissions do not establish procedural changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds DreamFusion and Wordrobe citations, removes Shoemake's quaternion-interpolation reference, and describes DressCode's sewing-pattern representation more explicitly. The central positioning relative to prior garment and VLM methods is retained.

P1.justification: The main-text exposition is substantially condensed and reorganized. GarmentCode and numeric-output explanations change order, training-data and implementation material moves into S1, and the reconstruction discussion is extensively streamlined. The supplement also gains a more subdivided results structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds supplementary Figures S2 and S4, relocates the reconstruction tables, and reverses the order of the sketch and editing figures. Existing visual content is largely retained, with revised captions and layout.

improvement.justification: The more precise loss specification, runtime breakdown, additional qualitative checks, and explicit representation limits modestly improve technical clarity and practical assessment. These gains are tempered by removal of failed-reconstruction exclusion and simulation details, which weakens reproducibility documentation. The principal benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
